**Test image observations:**
- Very young seedling (likely cotyledon stage) barely emerged from soil
- Brown/tan, collapsed, necrotic tissue at/near soil line
- Seedling appears to have failed emergence — rotted and shriveled
- Dark moist soil with crop debris visible

**Candidate analysis:**
- **Pythium damping off**: Pre/post-emergence damping off, seedlings collapse at soil level with water-soaked to brown rot — matches perfectly
- **Rhizoctonia**: Also causes damping off but typically shows distinct reddish-brown sunken cankers on hypocotyls of more developed seedlings
- **Phytophthora**: Usually affects more developed plants with stem lesions or wilting rows

**Reference comparison:**
- Pythium reference shows exactly this scenario: tiny seedlings at soil level with collapsing/brown cotyledons in dark moist soil — very high visual match
- Rhizoctonia reference shows more developed plants with distinct reddish lesions — less consistent
- Phytophthora reference shows more advanced plant death with standing wilted plants

The test image is a classic pre/post-emergence damping off at the seedling stage, matching Pythium damping off most closely.
